goal: A new employee at Muster AG answers one short English questionnaire in Lonio that asks each piece of information once, and only when a receiving party needs it for that person. From those answers Lonio records everything HR, Pensionskasse Muster and the Zurich source tax office need, including the derived insurance start date and the computed source tax tariff code.
context:
Today Muster AG's HR collects onboarding data for several receiving parties: the pension fund registration (Pensionskasse Muster portal), the source tax tariff (the Canton of Zurich calculator, which HR clicks through by hand) and HR's own needs, such as a complete postal address for posting documents. Pain points stated by the sources:
- The first working day is HR's 'number one' item, and it often moves (for example when an earlier exit is negotiated with the old employer). The pension fund insurance start date depends on it (F-hr_transcript-872bd7, F-hr_transcript-1d5c07, F-hr_transcript-e18e66).
- Incomplete addresses block posted documents (F-hr_transcript-c0fe95).
- The pension fund's required fields (Canton, Civil status, Spouse's date of birth) do not fit every case: employees abroad, registered partnerships, separated employees (F-pension_portal-b359c3, F-pension_portal-3d1ae4).
- HR's rule for who is subject to source tax took several corrections to state (F-hr_transcript-5af8d0, F-hr_transcript-550840).
- Determining the tariff code is a manual, multi-branch calculator walk-through: civil status, spouse employment, children, confession and the cross-border cases for Germany and Liechtenstein.

Lonio replaces this. It asks each item once and only when a party needs it (data minimisation, G-01). It derives values instead of asking for them (G-08). It computes the full tariff code itself (D-001).

Scope: the employee side of the questionnaire only (G-04, D-034).

Out of scope:
- transmission of the data to the parties
- HR screens and HR changes after submission
- AHV data and IT equipment (G-03)
- the photo for employee badges
- document uploads (D-035)
- income type and replacement income (D-006)
- special tariffs (D-009)

Decisions to follow:
- D-005: only 'C permit yes/no' is asked, never the permit type.
- D-003: registered partnership and separated are mapped provisionally for the fund.
- D-007: Liechtenstein residents may get 'in principle no source tax liability'.
- D-036, D-037: on submission, answers that no longer apply are discarded and the questionnaire becomes read-only. Derived results are always computed from the latest answers.

sections.title: Questionnaire flow overview
sections.purpose: Give the employee one English questionnaire with fixed steps, where each question appears only under its condition. At the end come the permit reminder and a submission that discards answers that no longer apply and makes the questionnaire read-only.

sections.title: Personal details and home address
sections.purpose: Collect the employee's name, date of birth and complete home address once. HR uses them to post documents and the pension fund to register the employee. The country of the address decides which later questions apply, and the canton is asked only of employees living in Switzerland.

sections.title: First working day and insurance start date
sections.purpose: Have the employee confirm their first working day, and derive the pension fund insurance start date from it instead of asking for it. The derived date always follows the latest first working day.

sections.title: Civil status and spouse data
sections.purpose: Ask the civil status once and map it both to the pension fund's list and to the calculator's civil status group. The spouse's or partner's date of birth is asked only where the fund needs it.

sections.title: Who is subject to source tax
sections.purpose: Decide from as few questions as possible whether the employee is subject to source tax: country of residence, Swiss citizenship, C permit (yes/no), and the spouse's citizenship, C permit and residence. Only employees subject to source tax are asked the tariff questions.

sections.title: Source tax tariff: denomination, spouse employment and tariff code
sections.purpose: Ask employees subject to source tax for their denomination and, if married or in a registered partnership, whether the spouse or partner works. Combine these with the child digit and the cross-border result into the computed Zurich tariff code that Lonio records for HR.

sections.title: Source tax tariff: children
sections.purpose: Ask employees subject to source tax whether they have children, then ask the calculator's questions once per child. Each child's answers decide whether that child counts toward the child digit, and whether it makes the tariff letter H for single employees. Before go-live, a domain expert checks the paths that were not observed in the calculator.

sections.title: Source tax: residence abroad and cross-border questions
sections.purpose: Derive the calculator's residence answer from the home address. Germany residents are asked the cross-border questions (daily return, certificate of residence, reasonable return, more than 60 non-return days), which decide the cross-border tariff. Liechtenstein residents are asked about daily return and more than 45 non-return days, which can lead to 'in principle no source tax liability' flagged for HR.
